title: AI adoption linked to increase in employment globally
source_used: King's College London press release, relayed by Mirage News (Phys.org pool link blocked: HTTP 403)
key_facts: A study by King's College London and Stanford University finds that firms recruit more senior staff and fewer junior staff after adopting generative AI.
Firm-level AI adoption is linked to around a 3.3% increase in the number of employees recruited overall.
Senior employment rises by 6.7% and junior employment falls by 2.5%, according to the study.
The study analysed 1.25 billion job advertisements and 158 million employee positions across 41 countries.
Firms count as adopters when their job ads say applicants will need to use generative AI.
Demand rose for senior employees and for workers in computer and mathematical occupations.
quote_evidence: We find a similar pattern in many labour markets, with firms employing fewer junior workers and more senior employees after adopting AI.
the findings suggest that generative AI is changing the mix of jobs within organisations rather than reducing overall employment.
why_it_matters_hint: The mix of jobs is shifting toward senior roles, even if overall hiring rises.
notes: Read on Mirage News, which republishes the King's College London release ('View in full' names kcl.ac.uk). The copy's year range is garbled ('2021 and 2016'), so no years are used. Paper: 'How Does AI Change Labor Demand? Evidence from 41 Countries' (Stanford and King's College London authors). Working paper status is not stated; no outside review reported, so PRELIMINARY.
